newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates ease, liquidity good.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates ease, liquidity good.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were steady to lower on Tuesday amid moderate demand thanks to relatively good liquidity, dealers said.
"The banks' accounts have thinned down somewhat, but demand and supply are pretty much balanced," dealer Radmila Nizetic told Reuters.
She put fresh loans at 32.5 million kuna, with call money loans at 8.0 percent accounting for three thirds of the trade by 0900 GMT.
One seven-day loan was granted at a lower 9.5 percent, compared to 11 earlier and the one-month price eased 50 basis points to 13 percent from last Friday.
Commercial banks' balances slipped to 580 million kuna on Monday, but none had any shortfalls. One bank borrowed 50 million kuna in overnight trade to maintain its reserves.
They had 21 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
